idiom_name: hand-written per-struct load/save functions plus a type-code switch
implementation_notes: C has neither classes nor mapper metaprogramming, so the mapper structure is entirely hand-written: one struct per table, one load/save function pair per struct, and a switch over the discriminator column that fills the right struct for a row (Single Table Inheritance). For Class Table Inheritance the 'mapper hierarchy' becomes a call chain - the subclass loader re-reads the base row (or the joined row) from the parent table and then fills the subclass fields from its own table; for Concrete Table Inheritance each loader is standalone. The mapping primitives are the database client's own: sqlite3_prepare_v2/sqlite3_step/sqlite3_column_* for SQLite, PQexec/PQgetvalue for libpq.
pitfalls: sqlite3_column_text returns a pointer into the statement buffer: copy the string before sqlite3_finalize or the next step, otherwise the mapped value dangles.
A NULL column arrives as a NULL pointer from sqlite3_column_text; passing it to strdup without a check crashes instead of mapping a missing subclass attribute.
The discriminator switch must handle unknown type codes explicitly; the common fall-through turns a data problem into a silently truncated base object.
There is no ownership convention to fall back on: the mapper must state who frees the strings it copies, or every load leaks.
